title: a formatter reserved fifteen bytes of tail room for a worst case needing sixteen
object: the caller-supplied output buffer of buf_len bytes, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a tail reservation one byte smaller than the longest thing that can still be appended
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: `oid_to_str_buf` no longer exists in v4.6.8:epan/to_str.c (`grep -c oid_to_str_buf` = 0), so the construct was REMOVED rather than fixed and the pinned code cannot carry the defect. A fix-reversal against history.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x1023a6, with supervise resolving `expect wsh_read_probe 0x102372` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the cursor is advanced by g_snprintf's RETURN value, which is the would-be length even when it truncated -- so the overrun is produced by a function that itself wrote nothing out of bounds. The fix names the worst case as a constant, `1 + 10 + 4 + 1`, which is the arithmetic that was never written down.
